entities.description: US television anthology series referenced once, noting Jyoti Amge's appearance as an actress in it.

In-app page comparing average male and female heights across countries with a sortable table, regional breakdowns, and a world heatmap. CONFLICT NOTE (resolved 2026-09-05, average-height-by-country page): originally registered translate:false, but the already-shipped nav/footer German translation (messages/de.json nav.averageHeightByCountry / footer.averageHeightByCountry) uses the localized form 'Durchschnittsgröße nach Land'. Updated to translate:true to stay consistent with the live navigation label, matching the same resolution already applied to 'Height Predictor', 'Ideal Body Weight Calculator', and 'Height Difference Calculator'.
A clinical height-prediction method combining bone age data with height-for-age tables to estimate remaining growth potential.
The Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, referenced here as one of the celebrity database's regional entertainment categories.
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, whose population data is used as a reference dataset for the percentile calculator.
The CDC's named growth-chart dataset/tool tracking average child height and weight by age, cited as a bibliography source and referenced inline on the height predictor page.
Nepalese man verified by Guinness World Records in 2012 as the shortest adult male ever documented, at 54.6 cm.
DC Comics/DC Entertainment, referenced as one of the fictional character library's franchise categories.
One of three ideal-body-weight estimation formulas (named after B. J. Devine) run side by side in the Ideal Body Weight Calculator.
The company providing Google Analytics, referenced in the privacy policy as the operator of that analytics service and its related policy documents.
Google's web analytics service, used by the site to collect standard usage data such as pages visited and general geographic region.
Google's official browser extension that lets visitors prevent Google Analytics from collecting data about their visit.
Google's named legal document governing use of Google Analytics, referenced as a link target in the privacy policy.
Google's own named privacy policy document, referenced as a link target for how Google handles analytics data.
The organization that verifies and certifies extreme human height records (tallest/shortest man/woman), cited multiple times in the extremes section.
One of three ideal-body-weight estimation formulas (named after G. J. Hamwi) run side by side in the Ideal Body Weight Calculator.
The formal/full product name of the tool, used interchangeably with the short brand name HeightComparison (e.g. in the privacy policy's introduction).

In-app calculator showing the exact gap between two heights in centimetres, inches, and percentage. CONFLICT NOTE (resolved 2026-09-04, height-difference-calculator page): originally registered translate:false, but the already-shipped nav/footer German translation (messages/de.json nav.heightDifferenceCalculator / footer.heightDifferenceCalculator) uses the localized form 'Höhendifferenz-Rechner'. Updated to translate:true to stay consistent with the live navigation label, matching the same resolution already applied to 'Height Predictor' and 'Ideal Body Weight Calculator'.

In-app calculator estimating a child's adult height using the Khamis-Roche formula and the Mid-Parental method. CONFLICT NOTE (resolved 2026-09-03, height-predictor page): originally registered translate:false, but the already-shipped nav/footer German translation (messages/de.json nav.heightPredictor / footer.heightPredictor) uses the localized form 'Größenwachstums-Rechner'. Updated to translate:true to stay consistent with the live navigation label rather than silently diverging from it on this page.
In-app calculator comparing a person's height and weight against WHO and CDC population data.
The product/brand name of this height comparison tool.
The site's domain name, referenced in the privacy policy as the URL where the tool is available. Never translated or altered.

In-app calculator that runs the Devine, Robinson, and Hamwi formulas side by side. CONFLICT NOTE (resolved 2026-09-03, ideal-body-weight-calculator page): originally registered translate:false, but the already-shipped nav/footer German translation (messages/de.json nav.idealBodyWeightCalculator / footer.idealBodyWeightCalculator) uses the localized form 'Idealgewichts-Rechner'. Updated to translate:true to stay consistent with the live navigation label, matching the same resolution already applied to the 'Height Predictor' entity.
In-app feature estimating height from an uploaded photo, including a morning height variation guide.
Indian actress from Nagpur who has held the Guinness World Record for shortest living woman since 2011, at 62.8 cm; also known for appearing in American Horror Story.
A clinical formula (named after researchers Khamis and Roche) for estimating adult height from a child's current measurements and parent heights.

A clinical formula (named after researchers Khamis and Roche) for estimating adult height without bone age testing, analyzing a child's age, height, weight, and parents' average height. Used as the display name of this method throughout the height predictor page (equivalent to the 'Khamis-Roche formula' entity already registered).

The named formula for estimating a child's adult height from parents' heights alone: (Father + Mother ± 5 in) ÷ 2. Displayed name used throughout the height predictor page (equivalent to the already-registered 'Mid-Parental method' entity).
A clinical method for estimating adult height from the average of both parents' heights, used alongside the Khamis-Roche formula.

One of four ideal-body-weight estimation formulas (named after researcher D. R. Miller, 1983) shown alongside Devine, Robinson, and Hamwi in the Healthy Weight by Height reference tables on the Ideal Body Weight Calculator page.
The CDC division credited as the data source for the growth-percentile chart on the height predictor page.

Global research collaboration (also referenced by its abbreviation 'NCD-RisC') that publishes the primary adult height dataset by country used throughout this page and cited in the references section.

The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, the CDC's national health survey program whose adult height distributions are the reference population for adult percentile comparisons on this calculator.
The image file format used for the tool's chart export, referenced when noting the export carries no watermark.
American man from Alton, Illinois, the tallest person in documented human history at 272 cm, died in 1940 aged 22.
One of three ideal-body-weight estimation formulas (named after researcher J. D. Robinson) run side by side in the Ideal Body Weight Calculator.
A clinical height-prediction method using bone age, current height, weight, and parental heights, primarily used in medical settings.
Turkish web developer and disability advocate, holder of the current living-record title for tallest woman at 215.2 cm, multiple Guinness titles.
Turkish man holding the Guinness record for tallest living man at 251 cm; his pituitary tumour was treated surgically, halting further growth.
The World Health Organization, whose population data is used as a reference dataset for the percentile calculator.
WHO's named growth-reference dataset for children aged 0-2, built from data collected across six countries, cited as the reference source for infant length percentiles.
Data publisher whose country-level average height figures are cited alongside NCD Risk Factor Collaboration data throughout this page.
Woman from Hunan Province, China, holder of the record for tallest woman in verified medical history at 246.3 cm; born 1964, died 1982 aged 17.
Nonprofit American academic medical center, cited as an authoritative medical reference for the age-2 doubling rule and mid-parental height formula on the height predictor page.
